title: Asked Claude to add a whole planet creator to my game that you can share, remix, and share.
author: niklasdaking
selftext:
Claude and I have been making a browser game called **Worldseed**. 

*retro-inspired massive open-world fantasy adventure that invites you to step off the beaten path and discover a world filled with possibilities.*

The new version (v46) adds a Maker that lets players create worlds inside the game and share them as text strings, it is short enough for a Discord message.

|The pipeline: Start a new world open the Maker, shape land, place towns, write simple rules, copy the world code. Anyone who gets it pastes it in, and their card says who made it. They can open it in the Maker and change it, or drop down to the planet and play out the adventure you created for them!|
|:-|


A few design questions I'm chewing on:

* The world is stored as text, not files. Is that a feature or a limitation? It feels like both.
* Rules are written in plain language, not a scripting language. Does that make it more accessible or more confusing?
* There is a limit to how much you can add to the world, is that good? or bad?

Would appreciate any thoughts from people building with AI tools in the loop.  
[https://generic-king.itch.io/worldseed](https://generic-king.itch.io/worldseed)
